supersedes.reason: The v1 set descended from the Accounts_staggering $200-per-$400 lifetime-gain ratchet. The 2026-08-30 independence decision cut that inheritance, and measurement showed the accumulation triggers were never the binding constraint: withdraw_500_after_1000_profit and minimum_only_when_eligible produced identical cohort results because the eight-trading-day and $26,600 balance gates bind first.

design_axis.summary: How the five capped payouts are spent before both the $1,500 cap and the Safety Net disappear, and how much cushion is left in the account.
binding_constraints_in_order: 8 completed PA trading days since activation or last executed request
5 of those days with realized net profit >= $50
payouts 1-5 capped at $1,500; no fixed cap from payout 6
design_axis.why_it_matters: The cap and the Safety Net both end on a payout counter, not on a dollar amount, so the number of early requests is a decision variable in its own right. A policy that takes the $500 minimum five times reaches uncapped withdrawals in the fewest eligible windows; one that waits for the full $1,500 extracts more per window but stays capped longer.

rule_kinds.maximum: request the largest amount baseline eligibility allows
rule_kinds.fixed: request a fixed amount; with require_full, wait until it is fully eligible
rule_kinds.fraction: request fraction x maximum eligible, floored at the $500 minimum

policies.label: $500 minimum whenever eligible
policies.description: Fastest burn through the five capped payouts and the largest retained account cushion. Reaches uncapped withdrawals in the fewest eligible windows.

policies.label: maximum eligible whenever eligible
policies.description: Extracts everything the rules allow at every opportunity. Strips the account to its floor and is the most exposed to a subsequent drawdown.

policies.label: $500 for payouts 1-5, then maximum
policies.description: Explicitly buys the uncapped regime with five minimum requests, then switches to maximum extraction. Tests whether the payout counter is worth optimizing directly.

policies.label: full $1,500 for payouts 1-5, then maximum
policies.description: Waits for the full capped amount at each of the first five requests, then switches to maximum. The opposite pole from rush_to_uncapped on the same axis.

policies.label: maximum without encroaching the safety net
policies.description: Maximum eligible subject to leaving at least $26,600 in the account, so the balance gate is never the reason the next request is refused. Trades extraction for immediate re-eligibility.

policies.label: half of the eligible maximum
policies.description: Requests 50% of what is allowed, floored at $500. The honest heir of the old 50% intent, expressed against the constraint that actually binds rather than against a lifetime-gain ratchet.

retained_mechanism.accumulated_profit_trigger_usd: Still implemented and unit-tested on PayoutPolicy, but no baseline policy uses it. Kept so the superseded v1 ratchet remains reproducible as a named sensitivity rather than being deleted from the code.
